summary: The note describes student-led health and wellness campaigns in schools across a district since September 2023, covering mental health, nutrition and fitness, inclusivity in health education, and digital wellness. Each campaign is tied to a specific school and student or teacher leaders, with quotes showing how the projects empower students and change habits. Personal testimonies from students such as Lucy Alvarez and Ben Thompson illustrate the real impact.
one_line: Student-led health and wellness campaigns in district schools since September 2023 are changing habits, reducing stigma, and building empathy and community.
key_facts: Since September 2023, numerous student-initiated health and wellness campaigns have appeared in schools across the district, supported by educators.
"Mind Matters Week" launched October 2, 2023 at Lincoln Middle School, organized by the student council led by eighth-grader Sarah Chen, to break the stigma around mental health.
Mind Matters Week featured workshops, guest speakers, relaxation spaces, psychologists, counselors and local celebrities, and led many students to form smaller support groups.
"Fuel Your Body, Fuel Your Mind" began September 15, 2023 at Washington High School with support from the school's sports teams, focusing on nutrition and physical activity.
Marcus Williams, a senior student-athlete, is a key proponent of the Washington High School campaign.
The Washington campaign included a "Healthy Eating Week" with a farmers' market, cooking demos, a cafeteria menu overhaul, dietitian talks, and fitness assessments.
"Everyone's Journey" started its inaugural event on November 6, 2023 at Valley View Elementary School, led by fifth-grade teacher Ms. Lydia Park and her students.

Jamie Peterson, who lives with diabetes, shares her health experience with classmates in Everyone's Journey, which includes student presentations, health story booths, and a "Day in the Life" simulation series.
Roosevelt Tech Magnet School students launched the online wellness platform "WellTech" on December 1, 2023, addressing internet usage, social media and mental health, cyberbullying, and screen time.
Omar Jackson, a junior, has been pivotal in running WellTech, which offers forums, blogs, live webinars, and streams with digital wellness experts, and connects students from various schools.
Lucy Alvarez, a Washington High junior, stopped skipping breakfast after the nutrition sessions and says she feels more focused in class.
Ben Thompson, a Thomas Jefferson High senior, says seeing friends speak out during Mind Matters Week gave him the courage to ask for help with anxiety.
Thomas Jefferson High School displays a poster reading "Your Health, Your Future."
